title: 古朗月行
title_en: An Old Song of the Bright Moon
author: 李白

text_note.zh: 原始文本第四句作“飞在白云端”，第六句作“桂树作团团”。课本和通行本作“飞在青云端”“桂树何团团”，这里用通行本。小学课本只选了前四句。
text_note.en: The corpus text has "white clouds" in line four and "the cassia tree grows round" with a different verb in line six. The textbook and usual text have "blue clouds" and "how round the cassia tree"; this page follows them. The primary school textbook includes only the first four lines.

readings.en: It reads shí, meaning to know.

readings.zh: 谁：口语常读 shéi，读诗时一般读 shuí。
readings.en: In speech it is often shéi; in poems it is usually read shuí.

glosses.en: xiǎo shí: when I was little.
shí: to know, to recognize.
hū zuò: to call it.

glosses.zh: 白玉盘：用白玉做的盘子。
glosses.en: bái yù pán: a plate made of white jade.
yí: to wonder whether, to suppose.

glosses.zh: 瑶台：传说中神仙住的地方，用美玉砌成。
glosses.en: yáo tái: in legend, the home of the immortals, built of fine jade.

glosses.zh: 青云端：青天白云的上面。端，顶端。
glosses.en: qīng yún duān: up above the blue clouds. Duān means the top or edge.

glosses.zh: 仙人垂两足：古代传说，月亮刚升起时，先看见月中仙人的两只脚，慢慢才看到整个月亮。
glosses.en: xiān rén chuí liǎng zú: an old legend says that when the moon rises, you first see the two feet of the immortal who lives in it, and only slowly the whole moon.

glosses.zh: 团团：圆圆的样子，枝叶茂密成团的样子。
glosses.en: tuán tuán: round and thick, like a ball of leaves.
hé: how!

glosses.zh: 捣药：把药材放在臼里用杵捶打。传说月亮上的白兔在捣长生不老的仙药。
glosses.en: dǎo yào: to pound medicine in a bowl. Legend says the white rabbit in the moon pounds a medicine that makes people live forever.
wèn yán: to ask.
yǔ shuí cān: for whom to eat.

glosses.zh: 蟾蜍：癞蛤蟆。古人看见月食，以为是月中的蟾蜍在啃食月亮。
glosses.en: chán chú: a toad. When people in old times saw an eclipse of the moon, they thought a toad in the moon was eating it.
shí: to eat away bit by bit.
yuán yǐng: the round moon.
dà míng: the great light, meaning the moon.
cán: broken, no longer whole.

glosses.zh: 羿：后羿，传说中善于射箭的英雄。
glosses.en: yì: Hou Yi, a hero in legend who was a great archer.

glosses.zh: 落九乌：射落九只乌鸦，就是射下九个太阳。传说古时天上有十个太阳，太阳里有三足乌，后羿射下了九个。
glosses.en: luò jiǔ wū: shooting down nine crows, meaning nine suns. Legend says there were once ten suns in the sky, each with a three-legged crow inside, and Hou Yi shot down nine of them.
tiān rén: heaven and earth, the gods and the people.
qīng qiě ān: peaceful and calm.

glosses.zh: 阴精：月亮。古人认为月亮是阴气的精华。
glosses.en: yīn jīng: the moon. People in old times thought the moon was the essence of the yin force.

glosses.zh: 沦惑：沉沦迷惑，这里指月亮被蚀，变得昏暗不明。
glosses.en: lún huò: sunk and confused; here it means the moon is eaten away and turns dim.
qù qù: go away, go away.
bù zú guān: not worth looking at any more.
qí rú hé: what can be done?
qī chuàng: sad and grieving.

glosses.zh: 摧心肝：让心肝都碎了，形容非常伤心。摧，毁坏。
glosses.en: cuī xīn gān: breaking one's heart, meaning very great sorrow. Cuī means to smash.

translation.en: When I was little I did not know the moon,
and called it a white jade plate.

translation.zh: 又怀疑它是瑶台上的仙镜，
translation.en: Or I thought it was the mirror from the jade terrace of the immortals,
flown up above the blue clouds.

translation.zh: 月亮升起时，先看到仙人垂下的两只脚，
translation.en: As the moon rises, first the immortal's two feet hang down,

translation.zh: 桂树长得多么圆圆满满。
translation.en: and how round and full the cassia tree grows.
The white rabbit has finished pounding its medicine,
but I ask, who is it for?

translation.zh: 蟾蜍一点点啃食着圆月，
translation.en: The toad eats away at the round moon,

translation.zh: 夜里明亮的月亮变得残缺了。
translation.en: and the great bright light of the night is broken.

translation.zh: 从前后羿射落了九个太阳，
translation.en: Long ago Hou Yi shot down nine suns,

translation.zh: 天上人间从此清平安宁。
translation.en: and heaven and earth became peaceful and calm.

translation.zh: 如今月亮被蚀得昏暗不明，
translation.en: Now the moon is sunk in darkness,

translation.zh: 还是走开吧，不值得再看了。
translation.en: so go away, it is not worth watching.

translation.zh: 心中的忧愁涌上来，该怎么办呢？
translation.en: When sorrow comes, what can I do?

background.zh: 《朗月行》是古代乐府诗的旧题目，李白借用它写了这首诗，所以叫“古朗月行”。写作时间不清楚。诗的前半写小孩眼中的月亮，后半写月食。一说诗中的蟾蜍蚀月，是暗指唐玄宗晚年被身边的人蒙蔽，朝政一天天变坏，所以诗人才这样忧伤。这只是后人的一种理解。
background.en: "Song of the Bright Moon" was an old title for folk-style ballads, and Li Bai used it for this poem, so it is called "An Old Song of the Bright Moon". We do not know when it was written. The first half shows the moon through a child's eyes; the second half describes an eclipse of the moon. One reading says the toad eating the moon hints at Emperor Xuanzong in his late years, misled by people around him while the government went bad, which is why the poet is so sad. This is only one later interpretation.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），唐代大诗人，人称“诗仙”。他一生特别爱写月亮，月亮在他的诗里有时是朋友，有时是故乡，有时是理想。这首诗把月亮的各种神话都写了进来，可以看出他丰富的想象力。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762) was a great Tang poet, called the Immortal of Poetry. All his life he loved to write about the moon. In his poems the moon is sometimes a friend, sometimes home, sometimes a dream. This poem gathers many old myths about the moon, and shows how rich his imagination was.

appreciation.zh: 开头四句最有名，写的是小孩子的眼睛：月亮是白玉做的盘子，又像神仙的镜子飞上了天。比喻又新鲜又可爱，一读就能看到那个画面。接着诗人把月亮的传说一个个请出来：仙人的脚、圆圆的桂树、捣药的白兔，月亮变得热闹又神奇。可是后来蟾蜍把月亮啃缺了，天变暗了。诗人想起后羿射日让天下太平，可现在没有这样的英雄。最后心情越来越沉重，悲伤得心都碎了。整首诗从天真的快乐，慢慢走到深深的忧愁。
appreciation.en: The first four lines are the most famous. They see through a child's eyes: the moon is a plate of white jade, or a fairy's mirror flown up into the sky. The comparisons are fresh and sweet, and you can picture them at once. Then the poet brings in the moon's legends one by one: the immortal's feet, the round cassia tree, the white rabbit pounding medicine. The moon becomes lively and magical. But then the toad eats the moon away and the sky grows dark. The poet remembers how Hou Yi shot down the suns and brought peace, but now there is no such hero. His mood grows heavier until his heart breaks with sorrow. The whole poem moves slowly from a child's joy to deep grief.
